title.zh: Weideman 有限谐波动理学色散

summary: Assemble the Maxwellian 3x3 kinetic tensor by finite cyclotron-harmonic sum with the source's positive near-zero kz clamp.

capability: Assemble the Maxwellian 3x3 kinetic tensor by finite cyclotron-harmonic sum with the source's positive near-zero kz clamp.
operation: assemble the fluid finite-harmonic kinetic tensor
SI species and wavepoint to dielectric and dispersion tensors and determinant
discovery.boundary: abs(kz)<1e-10 is replaced by +1e-10 before all resonant divisions

identity.relation: SI species and wavepoint to dielectric and dispersion tensors and determinant
identity.direction: SI species and wavepoint to dielectric and dispersion tensors and determinant
identity.definition: Sum harmonics -lmx..lmx using scaled Bessel Gamma terms and N=64 Weideman Z; D adds Maxwell curl terms to K and determinant=det(D).
identity.coordinates: wavevector in the x-z plane, with z parallel to B0
identity.boundary: abs(kz)<1e-10 is replaced by +1e-10 before all resonant divisions
assumptions: Input units and normalization follow the declared ports; no physical parameters are inferred.

inputs.name: B0
inputs.description: Background magnetic-field strength, setting the cyclotron frequency
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonzero; the cyclotron frequency is proportional to B0.

inputs.name: qs
inputs.description: Charge of each species, setting the sign of the cyclotron frequency
inputs.constraints: Finite; element count matches the other species arrays.

inputs.name: ms
inputs.description: Mass of each species, entering the thermal speed and cyclotron frequency

inputs.name: ns0
inputs.description: Absolute number density of each species, entering the plasma frequency

inputs.name: Ts0
inputs.description: Temperature of each species, already converted to kelvin under the source convention

inputs.name: f
inputs.description: Electromagnetic wave frequency, converted to angular frequency and then entering the resonance denominators and normalized refractive index
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonzero; omega is used as a divisor.

inputs.name: kz
inputs.description: Wavevector component parallel to the magnetic field, entering the parallel-resonance argument and the Maxwell curl term
inputs.constraints: Finite; before division the frozen source implementation clamps `abs(kz)<1e-10` (including `kz=0`) to `+1e-10`.

inputs.name: kx
inputs.description: Wavevector component perpendicular to the magnetic field, giving the Bessel argument and the refractive index

inputs.name: lmx
inputs.description: Bessel harmonic truncation order; the sum range is $|n|\le$ `lmx`
inputs.constraints: Optional, default 5 (matching the frozen source implementation); must be a nonnegative integer.

outputs.name: K
outputs.shape: `(3, 3)` complex matrix with component axis order x, y, z
outputs.constraints: Finite complex numbers; the off-diagonal antisymmetric pairs satisfy $K_{yx}=-K_{xy}$ and $K_{zy}=-K_{yz}$.

outputs.name: D
outputs.description: Dispersion tensor including the Maxwell curl term, that is, the matrix in which the dispersion relation is expressed
outputs.shape: `(3, 3)` complex matrix with component axis order x, y, z

outputs.name: determinant
outputs.description: Dispersion determinant $\mathcal{D}=\det D$; its zeros give the eigenmodes

outputs.name: omega
outputs.description: Angular frequency converted from the input frequency

outputs.name: wcs
outputs.description: Signed cyclotron frequency of each species
outputs.constraints: Nonzero, with the sign following qs.

outputs.name: lmx
outputs.description: Harmonic truncation order actually used, echoing the input

outputs.name: tensor_convention
outputs.description: Text label of the tensor convention, for the caller to check the sign convention

preconditions: Species arrays are finite, non-empty and shape-compatible; masses, densities and temperatures are positive, with nonzero charge and magnetic field.
The wavepoint and derived frequency/scales are finite and satisfy the selected numerical path domain.
supported: Assemble the Maxwellian 3x3 kinetic tensor by finite cyclotron-harmonic sum with the source's positive near-zero kz clamp.
excluded: Mode identification, root finding and accuracy outside the tested finite-harmonic or rational-pole approximation.
Inputs that violate the numerical domain or require a different tensor convention.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for declared invalid inputs; numeric conversion errors may propagate for unsupported Python objects.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the calculated tensor or function value is nonfinite.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative root solve is exposed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping is returned after an exception.

python.signature: evaluate_fluid_kinetic_dispersion_sum(*, B0, qs, ms, ns0, Ts0, f, kz, kx, lmx=5)

example.description: Evaluate the finite-harmonic Maxwellian tensor at one bounded wavepoint.
example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_fluid_kinetic_dispersion_sum
r=evaluate_fluid_kinetic_dispersion_sum(B0=1.0, qs=[-1.60217662e-19], ms=[9.1094e-31], ns0=[6.075e19], Ts0=[11604941.036704937], f=1e10, kz=1.0, kx=1.0); assert r['D'].shape==(3,3)
example.expected: Observed PASS: the finite-harmonic case returns finite 3x3 K and D tensors, determinant, species scales, and lmx=5.

scope: Declared source-method numerical case and relevant failure boundaries.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Bounded to the Maxwellian 3x3 kinetic tensor by finite cyclotron-harmonic sum with the positive near-zero kz clamp. Evidence: `test_fluid_spectrum_r43_variants.py` contains 6 test functions, 3 of which reference `evaluate_fluid_kinetic_dispersion_sum`, and is shared by 2 assets; only shared-file coverage is bound, so a pass is file-level rather than asset-isolated; the bounded example was executed by this audit. Oracle: bounded source-method parity. It does not establish mode identity, root finding, or accuracy outside the tested finite-harmonic approximation.
known_limitations: abs(kz)<1e-10 is replaced by +1e-10 before all resonant divisions
The finite harmonic sum uses analytic SciRel `Z` values; no finite-order Weideman special-function parity is claimed.
The finite harmonic cutoff `lmx` is caller-supplied; adequacy at larger `kx*rho` and root finding/mode identity are not established by the bound tests.
